content:
How should we make definitions for polynomials with integer coefficients? Currently I see two different ways in mathlib:
docs#Polynomial.Chebyshev.U and friends use ∀ (R : Type*) [CommRing R], Polynomial R. According to the module docstring, the advantage of this is that you don't need to map by Int.castRingHom R to transport it to a different ring.
docs#Polynomial.hermite uses Polynomial ℤ. The advantage that I see with this is that it isn't creating a definition family of one definition for every ring, see #mathlib4 > Mathlib's morphism hierarchy @ 💬.

In my opinion, we should go with the first. Taking from Jireh's very nice post in the linked thread, the disadvantage of the definition family for morphism classes is

Another issue is that we (and I have certainly been guilty of this before I saw the light) have implemented definitions which take a term of a morphism class (rather than a morphism itself) as a parameter. At first, this seems appealing, but the problem is that doing doesn't really create a single definition, but in some sense it is a definition schema, with one new definition for each instance of the morphism class. For example, since docs#AlgHom is an instance of docs#RingHomClass, and since docs#RingHom.ker takes a term of a RingHomClass as an argument, if f : A →ₐ[R] B is an algebra homomorphism we have both RingHom.ker f and RingHom.ker (↑f : A →+* B), and these are not trivially equal. Thus we would need additional API to go between them. So, we should restrict definitions to explicit morphisms, instead of morphism classes in order to avoid proliferating definitions.

but these considerations don't apply to the situation here, since there aren't nearly as many coercions of this form around types.
Also note that #41840 includes changing the Hermite example!
Agree, a ring already has coercions from Int to R, so no need to define it over Z when the more general definition works and is simpler.
